title: The Overlap Call
primary_metric: confirmed secondary cases found per test kit used

options.A: Test the union of both index patients' contact lists (Widest Net)
options.B: Test the intersection of both index patients' contact lists (Shared Risk)

balance_test.argument_A: Widest Net (union) tests 45 of 208 real contacts (Index Patients 698+686, post-D4 outlier drop) at the sourced 16.6% household close-contact secondary attack rate [S3], for an expected round(45x0.166)=7 confirmed secondary cases, a 7/45=15.56% per-kit yield -- and it structurally cannot miss an entire exposure category the way Shared Risk can.
balance_test.argument_B: Shared Risk (intersection) fully tests all 26 real dual-exposure contacts (post-D4 outlier drop) at the same sourced rate (MA2 -- no dual-exposure-specific rate exists), for an expected round(26x0.166)=4 confirmed secondary cases, a 4/26=15.38% per-kit yield, with 19 of the 45 allotted kits unused -- it spends every kit it does use on the highest-plausible-concentration group and never risks exceeding the weekly allotment.
balance_test.twist_effect: Mid-discussion, a countywide lab equipment failure cuts Priya's usable kit supply for the rest of the week from 45 to 27 (MA1 flexed downward by a real operational event, not a data change to either set). Widest Net's ratio drops to round(27x0.166)/27 = 4/27 = 14.81%, while Shared Risk's ratio is unaffected at 4/26 = 15.38% (it was already using fewer than 27 kits). The winner FLIPS from Widest Net (A) to Shared Risk (B), margin 3.85% -- the twist genuinely invalidates a room's pre-twist recommendation for A, and demonstrates live why P5's disclosed kits_per_week fragility (case.json.sensitivity_disclosure) is not just a theoretical sweep. See FACILITATOR.md.

margin_basis: margin_pct = percent difference between (secondary cases found in the union set / kits used testing the union) and (secondary cases found in the intersection set / kits used testing the intersection), computed with the D4 outlier (node 828) dropped from both real sets as the canonical resolution (consistent with real contact-tracing practice of investigating an implausible overlap before trusting it). Canonical set sizes: |A|=65, |B|=169, |A intersect B|=26, |A union B|=208. Kit allotment (MA1)=45/week. Secondary-case rate (Appendix B) = 16.6% [S3], applied to both groups per MA2 since no dual-exposure-specific rate exists. Counting convention (now stated explicitly in case.md Appendix B, not facilitator-only): expected cases = kits used x rate, rounded to the nearest whole person, before dividing by kits used. Sensitivity: if the outlier is instead kept (raw sizes |A|=66,|B|=170,intersect=27,union=209), margin widens to 5.00%, still favoring A -- both resolutions stay inside SPEC Sec.2's cap. See sensitivity_disclosure[] for the case's genuine, disclosed fragility to MA1/MA2 beyond the D4 outlier question.

assumptions.statement: The two index patients' contact lists are two real people's real friend circles from the Stanford SNAP ego-Facebook dataset (ego-node 698 = Index Patient 1, 66 contacts; ego-node 686 = Index Patient 2, 170 contacts), used as a structural stand-in for a contact-tracing network. No individually identifiable public-health contact-tracing dataset is used or implied to exist.
assumptions.why: A real, individually-identifiable public contact-tracing dataset does not exist publicly and should not -- it would be a privacy violation. The union/intersection/Venn-diagram math this case teaches is identical regardless of whether the underlying network represents friendships or disease contacts, so a real social graph is a legitimate, disclosed proxy rather than an invented one.

assumptions.statement: Priya's weekly test-kit allotment is fixed at 45 kits/week (MA1, case.md Appendix C).
assumptions.why: No public figure exists for a county unit's weekly test-kit supply. A real CDC report (MMWR 70(3), Jan 2021) [S5] gives a median contact-tracer caseload of 29 contacts/month -- a related but different quantity (staffing workload, not kit supply) over a different time unit (month, not week). 45/week is set at a plausible, comparable order of magnitude rather than derived arithmetically from that figure.
assumptions.sensitivity: The margin (1.11% canonical) is highly sensitive to this exact value -- see case.json.balance_test and FACILITATOR.md Socratic Q1/Q5 and the twist.

assumptions.statement: case-research searched for a published secondary attack rate specific to a 'dual index-patient exposure' contact and did not find one (two search attempts, including review of a real household-vs-non-household study [S4] from the same cohort). Per the plan flagged at write time, the sourced single-exposure rate [S3] (16.6%) is reused for both the union-only and intersection groups (MA2, case.md Appendix C), with the explicit disclosure that this likely understates the intersection group's true risk concentration -- every real source found shows closer/more concentrated exposure raising secondary attack rate, never lowering it.
assumptions.why: case-research considered two ways to derive a higher dual-exposure rate (an independence-based compound-probability calculation from [S3], and a proxy multiplier from [S4]'s household/non-household ratio) and rejected both: either approach forces the two options' per-kit ratios apart by 80%+ regardless of which ego-networks or kit allotment are chosen, which cannot be brought inside the SPEC Sec.2 ~20% cap by retuning a constraint -- manufacturing a plausible-looking compounding factor just to hit that gap would itself be the 'plausible number is not a true number' failure SPEC Sec.5 warns against. Reusing the honestly-sourced rate for both groups is the least-fabricated option; it also means the case's real decision has to rest on coverage guarantees, not an unfounded rate advantage.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public figure exists for a county unit's weekly test-kit supply. A real CDC report (MMWR 70(3), Jan 2021) [S5] gives a median contact-tracer caseload of 29 contacts/month -- a related but different quantity (staffing workload, not kit supply) over a different time unit. 45/week is set at a plausible, comparable order of magnitude, not derived arithmetically from S5.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The margin (1.11% canonical) is highly sensitive to this exact value -- see case.json.balance_test.twist_effect and FACILITATOR.md Socratic Q1/Q5.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Secondary-case rate applied to tested intersection (dual-exposure) contacts
modeling_assumptions.value: 16.6% (same as the sourced single-exposure rate, S3)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No published rate specific to a dual/compounded-exposure contact was found after two search attempts (see RESEARCH_LOG.md P09). Reusing S3's sourced single-exposure rate for both groups is the least-fabricated honest option; it is very likely an understatement of the intersection group's true risk, since every real source reviewed (including S4) shows closer/more concentrated exposure raising secondary attack rate, never lowering it.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Because both groups use the identical rate, the two plans' per-kit yields differ only by whole-number rounding of the expected case count over each plan's tested population size -- the case's real decision rests on coverage guarantees (full vs. partial), not on an unfounded rate advantage. See FACILITATOR.md Thread 1.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA1's 45-kits/week figure is a documented good-faith scenario constant sized against the closest real public analogue (S5's CDC monthly caseload figure) -- no county publishes an actual weekly test-kit-supply number, so this is a one-time proprietary-estimate exception, not a substitute for real sourcing. A fine-grained scan (cases/the-overlap-call/sensitivity_model.py) found the resolved winner is genuinely fragile to this exact value: because both plans apply the identical MA2 rate, each plan's per-kit ratio is mathematically just the rate itself in expectation, and the entire 1.11% canonical margin is a whole-number-rounding artifact of kits_per_week and pool size -- the winner oscillates between A, B, and an exact TIE repeatedly as kits_per_week moves through the range 20-59 (e.g. TIE at 20-26, B at 27, A at 28, B at 33, A at 34...), not a single clean flip point. This is disclosed, not eliminated: the case's own Twist (FACILITATOR.md) deliberately drops kits_per_week to 27 specifically to surface this fragility live in the room, and every facilitator running this case should treat kits_per_week as the single most load-bearing, least-robust number in the whole comparison.

MA2 (reusing the sourced single-exposure rate [S3] for the intersection group, because no dual-exposure-specific rate exists in the literature after two documented search attempts) is a one-time proprietary-inaccessible exception -- the true dual-exposure rate exists in principle but was not found publicly. cases/the-overlap-call/sensitivity_model.py's +/-50% sweep found rate_dual flips the winner to B at only +5% above baseline (17.43% vs. the stated 16.6%) and breaches SPEC Sec.2's 20% balance cap in both directions at the full +/-50% sweep (48.4% and 102.2%). This flip direction (a higher true dual-exposure rate favoring B) is the SAME direction the case's own MA2 disclosure already says is more plausible -- every real source reviewed (S3, S4) shows closer/more concentrated exposure raising secondary attack rate, never lowering it -- so this is a disclosed, honestly-flagged fragility pointing toward the case's own stated real-world caveat, not an arbitrary flip. A facilitator should be prepared for a room that argues from MA2's own text that B's true yield is understated and the real margin may already favor B.

facilitator.twist: See FACILITATOR.md -- mid-discussion, a countywide lab equipment failure cuts Priya's usable kit supply from 45 to 27 for the rest of the week. This genuinely flips the winner (Widest Net's ratio falls to 14.81%, below Shared Risk's unaffected 15.38%) and forces a room that already committed to Widest Net to reckon with why: spreading a fixed rate thin over a shrinking kit supply costs more, in rounding terms, than fully testing a smaller guaranteed-coverage group.
facilitator.sensitivity_note: This case involves disease exposure and limited test-kit capacity. Frame the stake as contacts protected, not cases missed, per SPEC Section 6's protection-over-destruction guidance. Facilitators should note this explicitly before the discussion.
